channel.title: Ayoub’s Growth Notebook
channel.description: 100 new practical English guides on growth and marketing.

item.title: Growth marketing plan: turn one business constraint into a clear roadmap
item.description: Build a growth marketing plan around the customer journey, one measurable constraint, a focused experiment and a budget the business can support.

item.title: Growth marketing vs performance marketing: where each one fits
item.description: Understand the difference between growth marketing and performance marketing, where they overlap and which responsibilities your business needs next.

item.title: Marketing growth audit: diagnose leaks before increasing spend
item.description: Run a marketing growth audit across positioning, acquisition, conversion, customer value and tracking, then turn the findings into a prioritized action list.

item.title: How to prioritize growth experiments when resources are limited
item.description: Prioritize growth experiments using business relevance, evidence, expected learning and implementation effort, with explicit guardrails and stopping rules.

item.title: North Star metric: choose a signal of recurring customer value
item.description: Choose a North Star metric that reflects customer value, connect it to input metrics and guard against activity that grows the number without helping users.

item.title: Marketing budget allocation: fund learning and proven demand separately
item.description: Allocate a marketing budget across reliable demand, controlled experiments and customer value, using contribution economics and explicit review rules.

item.title: Go-to-market plan template: connect audience, offer and distribution
item.description: Build a go-to-market plan with a clear customer trigger, differentiated offer, buying journey, distribution choices and measurable launch decisions.

item.title: Marketing positioning statement: make your offer easier to understand
item.description: Write a marketing positioning statement around customer context, alternatives, a useful outcome and credible proof instead of generic superlatives.

item.title: Customer research interview questions that reveal buying decisions
item.description: Use customer research interviews to understand triggers, alternatives, objections and buying steps without steering people toward the answer you want.

item.title: Growth loops vs funnels: choose the right model for your business
item.description: Compare growth loops and funnels, identify the mechanism that brings new demand back into a system and measure whether it produces valuable customers.

item.title: Paid media budget planning: estimate what a test can actually teach you
item.description: Plan a paid media test budget using conversion economics, buying lag, available demand and the evidence needed for a useful decision.

item.title: Google Ads search intent: match keywords to the buyer's next step
item.description: Group Google Ads searches by buying intent, separate education from evaluation and align the advertisement and landing page with the visitor's next decision.

item.title: Google Ads negative keyword strategy: remove irrelevant demand carefully
item.description: Build a negative keyword strategy from irrelevant search tasks, choose exclusions carefully and review whether valuable demand is being blocked.

item.title: Google Ads keyword match types: use control without confusing wording and intent
item.description: Understand broad, phrase and exact match as targeting choices, then evaluate real searches and customer quality instead of assuming exact wording control.

item.title: Google Ads Quality Score: diagnose relevance without chasing the number
item.description: Use Quality Score as a diagnostic for expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing-page experience, while keeping customer outcomes central.

item.title: Google Ads conversion tracking audit: verify the signal before changing bids
item.description: Audit Google Ads conversion actions for event meaning, duplicate firing, values, attribution timing and reconciliation with real customer records.

item.title: Brand vs non-brand search campaigns: report demand capture separately
item.description: Separate branded and non-branded search reporting so existing awareness, new demand, customer quality and incrementality are easier to evaluate.

item.title: Retargeting vs prospecting: compare reach, customer quality and added value
item.description: Compare retargeting and prospecting by audience relationship, customer outcomes and incremental contribution rather than treating attributed returns as directly comparable.

item.title: Campaign structure by customer intent: simplify decisions without losing relevance
item.description: Organize campaigns around distinct customer tasks, offers and business decisions, avoiding both excessive fragmentation and one undifferentiated campaign.

item.title: When to scale paid advertising: check quality, capacity and marginal economics
item.description: Decide when to scale paid advertising using mature customer outcomes, contribution, tracking reliability and operational capacity rather than a short winning streak.

item.title: Ad creative brief template: give the designer a customer problem to solve
item.description: Write an ad creative brief with a buying situation, customer tension, single promise, credible proof and a clear learning question.

item.title: How to write ad hooks that attract the right customer
item.description: Write advertising hooks around a recognizable customer situation, demonstrate the promise quickly and measure qualified progression rather than attention alone.

item.title: Feature-to-benefit copywriting: explain what changes for the customer
item.description: Translate product features into credible customer benefits by connecting capability, workflow change, outcome and evidence without inventing results.

item.title: Landing page message hierarchy: answer buying questions in the right order
item.description: Structure a landing page around offer understanding, customer fit, proof, purchase conditions and a clear next step without crowding the hero.

item.title: UGC ad brief: turn a creator's demonstration into useful customer evidence
item.description: Create a UGC ad brief that defines a real product experience, honest claims, required disclosures and a clear demonstration without scripting fake enthusiasm.

item.title: Marketing proof and trust: support claims without exposing confidential data
item.description: Choose marketing proof that supports a specific buying claim, explain its scope and protect confidential customer and company information.

item.title: Ad fatigue diagnosis: check the audience and offer before replacing everything
item.description: Diagnose suspected ad fatigue using exposure, response, customer quality and context, then choose whether to change the creative, audience or offer.

item.title: Ad-to-landing-page message match: keep the promise consistent after the click
item.description: Improve ad-to-landing-page message match by aligning the customer situation, promise, proof and next step without copying the ad word for word.

item.title: E-commerce offer design: make the purchase worthwhile without hiding the cost
item.description: Design an e-commerce offer around customer fit, product value, transparent conditions and contribution economics rather than an automatic discount.

item.title: Creative testing learning log: turn campaign results into reusable decisions
item.description: Build a creative learning log that records customer angles, hypotheses, outcome definitions, limitations and the next decision instead of only ranking assets.

item.title: SaaS activation rate: define first value before calculating the percentage
item.description: Define and calculate SaaS activation rate with a meaningful value event, eligible signup cohort, time window and checks for acquisition quality.

item.title: Time to value in SaaS: reduce the wait for a useful outcome
item.description: Measure SaaS time to value from a defined starting event to first useful outcome, then remove avoidable setup delays without hiding real requirements.

item.title: Free trial vs demo for SaaS: choose the next step that fits the buying job
item.description: Choose between a SaaS free trial, demo or guided pilot based on setup complexity, buyer roles, proof requirements and the path to meaningful value.

item.title: Product-qualified leads: turn useful behavior into a relevant sales conversation
item.description: Define product-qualified leads using customer fit, meaningful usage and a credible buying signal, then design a sales handoff that helps rather than interrupts.

item.title: Trial-to-paid conversion: diagnose the gap between first value and purchase
item.description: Calculate trial-to-paid conversion with mature cohorts and investigate activation, fit, pricing clarity and purchase friction before adding pressure.

item.title: Product-led vs sales-led growth: choose the motion around buying complexity
item.description: Compare product-led and sales-led growth through evaluation effort, buyer roles, setup requirements and economics, including when a hybrid approach makes sense.

item.title: SaaS cohort retention analysis: compare customers at the same age
item.description: Analyze SaaS retention by signup or customer cohort, define the recurring-value event and compare equivalent lifecycle periods without mixing immature groups.

item.title: SaaS churn analysis: separate cancellation reasons from the underlying problem
item.description: Analyze SaaS churn using customer cohorts, usage history, support context and payment outcomes, then distinguish avoidable friction from poor product fit.

item.title: SaaS pricing page experiments: clarify fit before testing persuasion
item.description: Test SaaS pricing-page clarity around plan fit, inclusions, limits and purchase conditions, with paid conversion and customer quality as connected outcomes.

item.title: SaaS expansion revenue strategy: grow accounts through additional value
item.description: Build a SaaS expansion strategy around real account needs, additional product value and successful rollout rather than upgrade prompts disconnected from usage.

item.title: E-commerce product page copy: answer the questions that block purchase
item.description: Write product page copy around the customer task, accurate inclusions, fit, proof and purchase conditions, with clear distinctions between digital and physical products.

item.title: Checkout abandonment analysis: separate unexpected costs from purchase friction
item.description: Diagnose checkout abandonment through stage counts, device behavior, purchase conditions and payment outcomes before assuming every departure needs a discount.

item.title: Abandoned cart recovery strategy: answer the obstacle before offering a discount
item.description: Build cart recovery around permission, accurate cart context, unresolved buying questions and completed customer outcomes instead of repeated discount reminders.

item.title: Average order value vs profit: bigger baskets can still create weaker economics
item.description: Compare average order value with contribution after product, fulfillment, discounts and other variable costs before evaluating an upsell or bundle as a win.

item.title: Product bundling strategy: combine products around one useful customer task
item.description: Design product bundles around complementary use cases, clear inclusions and contribution economics, with customer choice and post-purchase fit in view.

item.title: Free shipping threshold strategy: balance basket growth and delivery cost
item.description: Evaluate a free-shipping threshold through current basket distribution, contribution, delivery cost and customer behavior rather than copying another store's amount.

item.title: Digital product listing images: show the deliverable and explain the purchase
item.description: Create digital-product listing images that show the actual files or templates, clarify editing and delivery requirements and distinguish mockup props from inclusions.

item.title: Etsy listing title strategy: name the product clearly before adding search detail
item.description: Write Etsy listing titles with a recognizable product name and meaningful attributes, then keep the title, tags, preview and digital-delivery explanation aligned.

item.title: Canva template product marketing: sell the editable outcome accurately
item.description: Market Canva templates with actual previews, precise editing instructions, clear inclusions and honest requirements so buyers know what they can change.

item.title: E-commerce repeat purchase rate: measure returning buyers with a clear window
item.description: Calculate repeat purchase rate with a defined customer cohort and observation window, then interpret replenishment, product fit and acquisition quality.

item.title: Fully loaded customer acquisition cost: compare acquisition economics consistently
item.description: Calculate fully loaded CAC with an explicit cost scope, customer definition and reporting window, then distinguish it from media-only acquisition cost.

item.title: CAC payback period: estimate how long acquisition spending takes to recover
item.description: Estimate CAC payback using contribution rather than revenue, state recurring-value assumptions and avoid treating immature customer histories as guaranteed future returns.

item.title: Marketing attribution vs incrementality: distinguish credit from added impact
item.description: Understand attribution as a credit-allocation rule and incrementality as added impact, then choose evidence appropriate to the marketing decision.

item.title: UTM naming conventions: keep campaign links readable and reporting consistent
item.description: Build UTM naming conventions with consistent source, medium, campaign and content values, then verify destinations and avoid personal information in URLs.

item.title: GA4 event taxonomy: name customer behavior before instrumenting the site
item.description: Plan a GA4 event taxonomy with clear behavior definitions, useful properties and ownership, using recommended events where they fit the measurement need.

item.title: Marketing dashboard design: organize numbers around decisions
item.description: Design a marketing dashboard with a business question, stable metric definitions, mature outcomes and a clear distinction between diagnostics and results.

item.title: Conversion lag reporting: stop comparing mature results with unfinished journeys
item.description: Account for conversion lag between acquisition and customer outcomes, compare mature cohorts and label partial periods before making budget decisions.

item.title: Marketing data reconciliation: explain why platforms and business records differ
item.description: Reconcile marketing reports by checking event definitions, attribution, dates, currencies and duplicate records before adding platform revenue together.

item.title: A/B test results interpretation: distinguish observed differences from reliable learning
item.description: Interpret A/B tests with a defined primary outcome, valid allocation, sufficient observation and business guardrails, avoiding early peeking and causal overclaims.

item.title: Marketing ROI vs ROAS: keep revenue efficiency separate from economic return
item.description: Distinguish ROAS from a clearly defined marketing ROI calculation, include contribution and costs and separate attributed revenue from proven incremental value.

item.title: SEO content brief: turn search intent into a useful answer
item.description: Build an SEO content brief around a specific reader task, a distinct answer, useful evidence and related decisions instead of a keyword repetition target.

item.title: Topic clusters and internal linking: connect distinct questions around one subject
item.description: Organize related articles into topic clusters with useful hubs, descriptive internal links and distinct page purposes, avoiding arbitrary keyword-based connections.

item.title: Content refresh audit: update the answer when the underlying information changes
item.description: Audit existing content for factual changes, unclear answers, broken links and overlapping scope, then make meaningful updates rather than changing dates alone.

item.title: SEO titles and meta descriptions: explain the page's answer clearly
item.description: Write unique page titles and meta descriptions that identify the reader's question and useful answer, while recognizing that search engines may display different wording.

item.title: Technical SEO for a static website: make useful pages easy to access and understand
item.description: Audit a static website for valid URLs, crawlable navigation, canonical metadata, sitemap coverage, readable mobile layout and indexable article content.

item.title: Multilingual SEO and hreflang: connect real translations without false equivalents
item.description: Use separate language URLs, accurate hreflang relationships and localized navigation, linking only actual equivalent translations rather than unrelated collection pages.

item.title: AI search visibility for a small business: make useful evidence discoverable
item.description: Improve discoverability for AI-assisted search with accessible pages, direct answers, clear business identity and evidence, while separating visibility from guaranteed citations.

item.title: Answer engine content writing: make the answer clear without flattening the nuance
item.description: Write answer-focused articles with a direct opening, explicit definitions, scoped examples, useful questions and visible supporting evidence for readers and search systems.

item.title: SEO vs paid search: match the channel to the business question
item.description: Compare SEO and paid search by time horizon, control, customer intent and economics, then design a complementary plan instead of choosing from generic claims.

item.title: Search Console content analysis: turn query evidence into better pages
item.description: Use Search Console query and page evidence to investigate visibility, intent mismatch and content opportunities, with care around averages and changing search appearances.

item.title: Lifecycle marketing strategy: communicate around the customer's next useful step
item.description: Build a lifecycle marketing strategy around first value, recurring use and relevant customer needs, with clear triggers, ownership and outcome measures.

item.title: Behavior-based email segmentation: group people by a relevant next task
item.description: Segment email audiences by meaningful behavior and customer context, keeping definitions, permissions, exclusions and message purpose clear.

item.title: Welcome email sequence: help a new customer begin instead of telling the whole brand story
item.description: Design a welcome sequence around access, first useful action and realistic expectations, with behavior-based stopping and clear support routes.

item.title: Reactivation campaign strategy: help inactive customers rediscover relevant value
item.description: Design reactivation campaigns for inactive but eligible customers, distinguish changed needs from usage obstacles and measure resumed value rather than opens alone.

item.title: Customer win-back strategy: invite departed customers back for a real reason
item.description: Build win-back campaigns around departure reasons, genuine changes and customer fit, with clear purchase conditions and retained outcomes after return.

item.title: Post-purchase communication: reduce uncertainty after the customer says yes
item.description: Design post-purchase messages around confirmation, access or delivery, first use and support, keeping promotion secondary to the customer's current task.

item.title: Customer referral program design: reward a useful recommendation, not invitation volume
item.description: Design referrals around satisfied customers, suitable new buyers, clear terms and contribution, with guardrails for abuse and low-quality acquisition.

item.title: Loyalty program value vs discounts: give customers a relevant reason to return
item.description: Evaluate loyalty programs through useful customer benefits, contribution and repeat behavior, distinguishing rewards for existing habits from added value.

item.title: Lifecycle trigger audit: prevent automation from sending the wrong message
item.description: Audit automated lifecycle triggers for event meaning, current state, exclusions, timing and ownership before scaling communication.

item.title: Marketing automation and human handoff: know when a conversation needs judgment
item.description: Design automation with clear scope, accurate context and a human handoff for uncertainty, exceptions and customer situations that require judgment.

item.title: Morocco COD unit economics: calculate contribution from delivered orders
item.description: Model cash-on-delivery economics with delivered revenue, dispatch and return costs, product costs and media spending, using explicit assumptions.

item.title: COD order confirmation workflow: verify intent and expectations clearly
item.description: Design a COD confirmation workflow around accurate order details, customer intent, delivery expectations and a reliable operational handoff.

item.title: COD delivery rate: use a clear denominator and mature courier outcomes
item.description: Calculate COD delivery rate with a defined dispatched cohort and observation window, distinguishing courier completion from end-to-end order performance.

item.title: COD refusal and return analysis: diagnose the reason before blaming the audience
item.description: Analyze COD refusals and returns by customer expectations, product, region and fulfillment evidence, connecting the diagnosis to contribution and appropriate repairs.

item.title: Darija vs French marketing in Morocco: choose language around the buying situation
item.description: Test Darija and French messaging around audience comprehension, product terminology and customer context, keeping the offer and measurement comparable.

item.title: WhatsApp e-commerce order follow-up: keep messages accurate and useful
item.description: Plan WhatsApp order follow-up with suitable permissions, accurate order state, helpful questions and a clear human route for exceptions.

item.title: Local landing pages for Morocco: explain real service conditions in the right language
item.description: Build local landing pages around genuine customer and service differences, with accurate delivery, language, offer conditions and useful evidence.

item.title: COD lead quality vs cost: evaluate orders through confirmation and delivery
item.description: Compare COD acquisition sources using confirmed, delivered and collected outcomes, showing why a cheap order-form lead can still create expensive demand.

item.title: Marketing and logistics alignment: make the delivery promise match reality
item.description: Align ads, product pages, confirmation and delivery operations so customers receive consistent expectations and growth does not exceed fulfillment capacity.

item.title: COD order dashboard: show progression, pending outcomes and contribution
item.description: Build a COD dashboard that separates created, confirmed, dispatched, delivered and collected orders, with mature cohorts and explicit cost definitions.

item.title: Mobile app growth strategy: connect discovery to a useful first session
item.description: Build an app growth strategy around audience fit, store-page expectations, onboarding, recurring value and acquisition economics rather than install volume alone.

item.title: App installs vs activation: measure the difference between access and value
item.description: Distinguish app installs from activation with a useful first-value event, eligible cohort and outcome window, then compare acquisition quality fairly.

item.title: App Store optimization for conversion: make the product page explain real fit
item.description: Improve app-store product-page conversion with accurate messaging, representative screenshots and a coherent first-use promise, measuring downstream quality as well as installs.

item.title: Apple Search Ads keyword intent: connect store searches to the app's useful task
item.description: Evaluate Apple app-store search advertising around customer tasks, accurate product-page expectations and activated outcomes rather than keyword volume alone.

item.title: Google App campaigns measurement: choose an outcome beyond the download
item.description: Plan Google App campaign measurement with valid conversion events, acquisition context and downstream user value, using current platform options appropriately.

item.title: App onboarding drop-off: find the step that blocks the first useful action
item.description: Diagnose app onboarding drop-off through step definitions, customer intent, permission context and useful completion, avoiding changes that merely inflate tutorial metrics.

item.title: Day-one and day-seven app retention: define the return behavior and window
item.description: Interpret day-one and day-seven app retention with explicit cohort, return-event and day definitions, comparing products according to their natural use cycle.

item.title: Mobile app referral loops: design sharing around real user value
item.description: Build app referral loops with a useful sharing moment, recipient context and activation quality, keeping incentives and privacy aligned with the product.

item.title: App push notification strategy: send a useful prompt, not a return-at-any-cost message
item.description: Plan push notifications around permission, timely customer tasks and accurate app context, measuring useful completion and customer response rather than opens alone.

item.title: Mobile app growth reporting: connect acquisition, activation and retained value
item.description: Build an app growth report with consistent acquisition cohorts, meaningful activation, return definitions and business costs, showing partial data and attribution limits.
